seo_title: THT Odd-Form Insertion Solution: S7900VI with Lead Clinching for Smart Lighting Control Boards | Southern Machinery
seo_desc: S7900VI odd-form insertion cell for relays, fuses, MOVs, MOSFETs, capacitors and Faston terminals on 3 control boards: 91 insertion points, cycle 30 s → 8 s without clinching, 4.7× manual output.
seo_keys: odd form insertion machine, THT auto insertion, lead clinching, relay insertion, Faston terminal insertion, axial resistor insertion, S7900VI, smart lighting control PCB
ans_h2: Can one machine insert relays, fuses, MOVs, MOSFETs and Faston terminals on lighting control boards?
ans_p: Yes. One S7900VI 6-head odd-form inserter between an SLD250 magazine loader and an SLUD250 unloader covers 3 boards with 91 insertion points, fed by 2 tube, 1 bulk belt, 4 radial, 1 axial and 1 reel-terminal feeder. Board 1 takes 30 s with lead clinching and 8 s without; the proposal rates the machine at 4.7× manual insertion.
qf1v: Smart lighting control boards (3 boards, 2 of them 12-up panels)
qf2v: Relays, fuses, MOVs, MOSFETs TO-220F, electrolytic and film capacitors, axial resistors, Faston terminals
qf3v: S7900VI, 6 heads, 4 grippers + 1 nozzle, lead clinching
qf4v: Board 1: 120 boards/h with clinching, 450 without; Board 3: 6,849 → 20,438 a month
qf5v: Tube STF201 ×2, belt SMVF01, radial SRF1001 ×4, axial SAF1001, reel terminal SRT201
qf6v: Customer proposal 2026-01-20; open points listed on this page
blog_lead: Eight short reads from this project: what to measure, what to decide and what to send before you buy.
faq_h2: Questions buyers ask about this cell
q1: Why clinch the leads at all?
a1: Clinched leads hold relays, MOVs and capacitors flat during wave soldering, so they do not float or tilt. The price is about 2 s per clinched point.
q2: How much cycle time does clinching cost?
a2: Board 1 goes from 8 s to 30 s per board and Board 3 from 62 s to 185 s. Clinch only the parts that really float.
a3: Manual insertion at about 1,000 insertions per hour. The proposal rates the S7900VI at 4,700 per hour, 4.7× the manual rate.
a4: 2 STF201 tube feeders, 1 SMVF01 belt feeder for bulk parts, 4 SRF1001 radial tape feeders, 1 SAF1001 axial feeder and 1 SRT201 reel terminal feeder.
q5: Do my boards need design changes?
a5: Check hole sizes for clinched leads (lead below 1.0 mm, at least 2 mm protruding), board edges for the conveyor and panel size within 410 × 350 mm.
q6: What do you need to start?
a6: Bare PCBs, every component in its real packaging, the final BOM and your decision on which parts are clinched. We then run a sample test and send video and cycle data.
ct_h2: Send your boards for a sample run
ct_p: Bare PCBs, components and BOM are enough to start.
bl1t: Your relays are the slowest part of the board
bl1s: Odd-form parts eat most of the manual insertion time.
bl1p1: On a small control board, two relays, two MOVs and two MOSFETs take longer by hand than all the chips around them.
bl1p2: Operators tire, polarity mistakes slip through and parts tilt in wave soldering.
bl1p3: Count the odd-form insertion points per board, the panel size and the packaging of each part before you look at machines.
bl1p4: Here 3 boards carry 91 points; one S7900VI cell with 9 feeders covers all of them.
bl1p5: Re-count the points each time the BOM changes; one new part type can mean a new feeder.
bl1p6: Send us your BOM and we will map each part to a feeder.
bl2s: Lead clinching costs about 2 s per point.
bl2p1: Board 1 runs in 8 s without clinching and 30 s with it.
bl2p2: Clinching every lead because one part floated once quadruples the cycle.
bl2p3: List which parts tilt or float in wave soldering today; clinch only those.
bl2p4: The S7900VI clinch unit offers outward, inner, circular and 2-turn bends at 15–30°.
bl2p5: Review float defects after every new lot of parts.
bl2p6: Mark the parts you want clinched on the BOM and we will recalculate the cycle.
bl3t: Panels multiply every second you save
bl3s: On a 12-up panel, 1 s per board is 12 s per panel.
bl3p1: Board 1 drops from 360 s to 96 s per panel without clinching.
bl3p2: Small savings per board are easy to ignore.
bl3p3: Always convert board cycle to panel cycle and then to boards per hour.
bl3p4: At 8 s per board the cell makes 450 Board 1 boards per hour; at 30 s, 120.
bl3p5: Re-check the panel layout when the PCB is revised.
bl3p6: Send the panel drawing and we will check fit within 410 × 350 mm.
bl4s: The machine waits for the slowest feeder.
bl4p1: Relays arrive in trays, fuses on tape, MOVs and MOSFETs in bulk, Faston terminals on reels.
bl4p2: Each packaging type needs the right feeder, or the head waits.
bl4p3: Match every part to tube, bulk belt, radial, axial or reel feeder before quoting.
bl4p4: This cell uses 2 STF201, 1 SMVF01, 4 SRF1001, 1 SAF1001 and 1 SRT201.
bl4p5: Track refill intervals per feeder in the first month.
bl4p6: Tell us how each part is packed today.
bl5s: 45 terminals per board is a job for a reel feeder.
bl5p1: Board 3 carries 45 Faston terminals, 14 film capacitors and 14 axial resistors.
bl5p2: By hand that is 73 placements per board and sore thumbs.
bl5p3: Use a reel terminal feeder and a matching gripper; check terminal pitch and press-in force.
bl5p4: Board 3 runs in 62 s without clinching, 20,438 boards a month on two shifts.
bl5p5: Check terminal height after soldering on the first lots.
bl5p6: Send a terminal reel and a bare board for a test.
bl6s: Lead checks before insertion stop bent-lead rejects.
bl6p1: Odd-form parts arrive with bent or short leads more often than you think.
bl6p2: A missed lead means a lifted part or a rework station.
bl6p3: Check every part's leads before it reaches the board.
bl6p4: The S7900VI captures leads with six cameras in 0.5 s, then inserts with controlled force up to 29.4 N.
bl6p5: Review vision rejects weekly to spot a bad supplier lot.
bl6p6: Ask for the vision test video of your parts.
bl7s: Write the formula next to every capacity figure.
bl7p1: Proposals often reuse a summary from another board.
bl7p2: Here the Board 2 summary repeats 73 % and 3.75×, while 24 s → 7 s gives 71 % and 3.43×.
bl7p3: Recompute every reduction and every boards-per-hour figure from the cycle time.
bl7p4: This page lists each such point under Accuracy & open points.
bl7p5: Repeat the check after the sample run with measured times.
bl7p6: Ask us for the calculation sheet.
bl8s: Three steps, about a month for custom parts.
bl8p1: A proposal is a plan, not a measured result.
bl8p2: Without samples, gripper and clinch choices stay guesses.
bl8p3: Send samples, confirm clinch and bend points, then watch a sample run.
bl8p4: Southern Machinery customises grippers, feeders and clinch units in about a month and ships spare parts in one day.
bl8p5: Keep a list of part changes for each new board revision.
bl8p6: Email info@smthelp.com or message us on WhatsApp.
